issue.title: ServerGoalHandle may throw from a destructor
issue.body:
### Generated by Generative AI

_No response_

### Operating System:

ubuntu 22

### ROS version or commit hash:

humble

### RMW implementation (if applicable):

_No response_

### RMW Configuration (if applicable):

_No response_

### Client library (if applicable):

rclcpp_action

### 'ros2 doctor --report' output




### Steps to reproduce issue

Destructor of ServerGoalHandle may throw an exception from `on_terminate_state` callback https://github.com/ros2/rclcpp/blob/rolling/rclcpp_action/include/rclcpp_action/server_goal_handle.hpp#L250, callback is defined here https://github.com/ros2/rclcpp/blob/rolling/rclcpp_action/include/rclcpp_action/server.hpp#L511. Since destructors are `nothrow` in C++11 this results in termination of a program.

### Expected behavior

destructors should not throw

### Actual behavior

.

### Additional information

PS: the goal should be aborted on destruction rather than canceled to match design spec
```
ABORTED - The goal was terminated by the action server without an external request.
CANCELED - The goal was canceled after an external request from an action client.
```
https://design.ros2.org/articles/actions.html

comments.body:
@asherikov thanks for creating follow-up issue and description.

i do agree with you that it should `abort` the goal instead of `cancel`. this is kind of surprise for action client, since it never requests the cancel.

> Since destructors are nothrow in C++11 this results in termination of a program.

I am not quite following this line, can you rephrase this?
my understanding is that, destructors are not always `nothrow` in C++11.
They are only `noexcept(true)` if all subobjects’ destructors are also non-throwing.

comments.body:
Based on the current implementation, the lifecycle of the ServerGoalHandle is controlled by the user.   

In Action Server, only a weak pointer to `ServerGoalHandle` is held.
https://github.com/ros2/rclcpp/blob/82696f6e5785081a0cd8bbe3b688e720dc5d08b4/rclcpp_action/include/rclcpp_action/server.hpp#L602-L605

When the user's handle_goal callback function returns "accepted," the server will create a `ServerGoalHandle` and pass it as a parameter to the handle_accepted callback function registered by the user.  That is, the user is responsible for managing the ServerGoalHandle.
https://github.com/ros2/rclcpp/blob/82696f6e5785081a0cd8bbe3b688e720dc5d08b4/rclcpp_action/include/rclcpp_action/server.hpp#L545-L552

It's easy to reproduce this issue by modifying fibonacci_action_server.cpp as follows.
rclcpp::Rate loop_rate(1); => rclcpp::Rate loop_rate(0.01);
https://github.com/ros2/demos/blob/472a4796bb838906a286c8c00260169873255e59/action_tutorials/action_tutorials_cpp/src/fibonacci_action_server.cpp#L148

I haven't come up with a good solution to change action server.   
To ensure that the ServerGoalHandle is properly abort, my current idea is for the user to register a cleanup function through context::add_pre_shutdown_callback(), so that the ServerGoalHandle is correctly abort and the user process is aware that it is about to shut down before shutdown. Since ServerGoalHandle is abort, the destructor of ServerGoalHandle will do nothing.
comments.bodyHTML:
Based on the current implementation, the lifecycle of the ServerGoalHandle is controlled by the user.

In Action Server, only a weak pointer to ServerGoalHandle is held.

rclcpp/rclcpp_action/include/rclcpp_action/server.hpp

Lines 602 to 605 in 82696f6

using GoalHandleWeakPtr = std::weak_ptr<ServerGoalHandle<ActionT>>;
/// A map of goal id to goal handle weak pointers.
/// This is used to provide a goal handle to handle_cancel.
std::unordered_map<GoalUUID, GoalHandleWeakPtr> goal_handles_;

When the user's handle_goal callback function returns "accepted," the server will create a ServerGoalHandle and pass it as a parameter to the handle_accepted callback function registered by the user. That is, the user is responsible for managing the ServerGoalHandle.

rclcpp/rclcpp_action/include/rclcpp_action/server.hpp

Lines 545 to 552 in 82696f6

goal_handle.reset(
new ServerGoalHandle<ActionT>(
rcl_goal_handle, uuid, goal, on_terminal_state, on_executing, publish_feedback));
{
std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(goal_handles_mutex_);
goal_handles_[uuid] = goal_handle;
}
handle_accepted_(goal_handle);

It's easy to reproduce this issue by modifying fibonacci_action_server.cpp as follows.
rclcpp::Rate loop_rate(1); => rclcpp::Rate loop_rate(0.01);
https://github.com/ros2/demos/blob/472a4796bb838906a286c8c00260169873255e59/action_tutorials/action_tutorials_cpp/src/fibonacci_action_server.cpp#L148

I haven't come up with a good solution to change action server.
To ensure that the ServerGoalHandle is properly abort, my current idea is for the user to register a cleanup function through context::add_pre_shutdown_callback(), so that the ServerGoalHandle is correctly abort and the user process is aware that it is about to shut down before shutdown. Since ServerGoalHandle is abort, the destructor of ServerGoalHandle will do nothing.

comments.body:
> my understanding is that, destructors are not always nothrow in C++11.

Yes, but destructors must be marked as `noexcept(false)` explicitly. Anyway my test get terminated, https://www.en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/language/destructor.html:
> a destructor may terminate by throwing an exception (this usually requires it to be explicitly declared noexcept(false))(since C++11), however if this destructor happens to be called during stack unwinding, std::terminate is called instead.

In any case, the destructor should try-catch to be safe https://clang.llvm.org/extra/clang-tidy/checks/bugprone/exception-escape.html

PS: it seems that explicit destruction of action server before destruction of the goals prevents attempts to cancel the goals and can be used as a workaround.

comments.body:
PR #2953 fixes a crash we are reproducing reliably on Jazzy. 

A duplicate UUID  is **a** specific trigger for the destructor-throw bug.

Can this please be backported to jazzy.
